newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Christmas violence kills 37 in Colombian capital.
newsitem.headline: Christmas violence kills 37 in Colombian capital.

text.p: At least 37 people were killed in street fights, stabbings and other violence in Bogota on Christmas Eve and early Christmas Day, city officials said.
Mayor Antanas Mockus blamed the violence on "undisciplined citizens" who flouted his calls for the capital's inhabitants to cut down on alcohol consumption during the festive season.

The 37 killings in just over 12 hours, however, was an improvement on recent years when as many as 100 people have been killed in a single Christmas Eve in the Colombian capital, which has a population of about eight million.
In January to November this year more than 3,000 people were murdered in Bogota, according to police statistics.
At least 10 people were reported murdered overnight in Cali, Colombia's second largest city, where a bomb exploded early on Christmas Day, causing no injuries, police said.
In Bucaramanga, in northern Colombia, five people were seriously wounded when a motorcyclist lobbed a hand-grenade at them as they stood at a street corner on Christmas Eve, police said.
